packs.title: River to Lagoon
packs.promise: Follow Valencia from its historic centre through the Turia corridor to the coast and Albufera.

q.s: Choose a stall product and record its stall, name and one supported detail.
st: Enter through a public market entrance during current opening hours, or open the market’s official online stall directory.
Choose one stall product; record the stall name, product name and one visible or published product detail.
Label each detail as seen on site or read in the official directory; include origin or season only when the display or directory states it.

q.s: Follow a named Turia Garden segment and chart how its bridge crossings connect the former riverbed to street level.
st: Enter the Turia Garden at Pont de la Trinitat and follow the marked garden path toward Pont de les Flors.
Choose one bridge crossing and note how the garden path connects to street level on each side; identify a ramp or stair only if visible.
Draw a simple path-and-crossing diagram from the Pont de la Trinitat start toward Pont de les Flors; mark the route you actually used.

q.s: Compare the Hemisfèric’s curve with its reflection from a public path.
st: Stand on a public path facing L’Hemisfèric and its reflecting pool.
Trace the building’s outer curve and one reflection or shadow visible at the time.
Make a two-part drawing or written comparison of the built curve and its changing reflection; label the time.

packs.title: Cabanyal and Marina
packs.promise: Spend one or two afternoons reading Valencia’s former fishing quarter through streets, tiles and the sea edge.

q.s: At Cabanyal Market, compare a current public food display with the district’s documented fishing history.
st: Start at the public entrance of Mercado del Cabanyal, Carrer de Martí Grajales 4; enter only during open hours.
Find one public display related to seafood or another local product; record exactly what you see without claiming its origin.
Read the official market account and write one supported connection and one difference between that account and your observation.

q.s: Borrow a visible motif on Carrer de la Reina, then give it a new four-part rhythm on paper.
st: Choose one residential façade visible from the public pavement on Carrer de la Reina and note one repeated tile shape or border.
Draw the observed motif once as your reference; do not assume its age or meaning.
Use that shape in a new sequence of four units. Rotate, mirror or space it differently to make your own arrangement.
Label the original motif and your invention separately, then give your sequence a short name.

q.s: Find one public activity space and one visitor service at Cabanyal beach.
st: Start on the Cabanyal public promenade and look toward the open beach.
Find one visible activity space, such as a sports field or children’s play area, and one visitor service, such as seating, a marked access facility or an open rental point.
Write what each supports, where it sits relative to the promenade, and which details were actually visible on the day.
